rows.rationale: The clause states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible, which contradicts the rejection based on transformer capacity. | The cumulative solar capacity (95kW) is 95% of the 100kVA transformer, but the cited clause says up to 150kW is deemed feasible. | While a check meter is missing for a 45kW system, the decision is flagged because the transformer capacity rule is contradictory.

The proposed capacity is 45.00 kWp, which is below the 50kWp threshold required for a check meter under KA-C5-006#cl-18. | The cumulative solar capacity (95kW) is 95% of the 100kVA transformer, but Note ii states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible.
The rule states check meters are mandatory for capacity > 20 kW, but the application's proposed capacity is exactly 20.00 kWp, making the meter optional.
The rule mandates check meters for systems > 20 kW, but the application's sanctioned load is 25 kW, making the check meter requirement applicable despite the 20 kWp DC capacity.

The decision is premature because the technical feasibility outcome is still 'Not communicated by the licensee' per the DISCOM portal status. | The generator failed to consider the rule stating installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a formal feasibility report.
The cited clause was superseded by GJ-C3-003, which mandates 1.0 and 0.5S accuracy instead of 0.2s. | The generator failed to apply the updated accuracy requirements from the 2020 amendment.
The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8, which allows capacity up to 5 times the sanctioned load (15,000 kW), making the 12,000 kW proposal compliant.
The proposed 1.0 kWp capacity does not exceed the 2.0 kW sanctioned load, so the rejection is incorrect.

The proposed 1.00 kWp capacity violates clause 5.1's proviso which requires a minimum capacity of 1 kWp, but the generator failed to address the 2015 regulation's minimum requirement. | The generator failed to consider UP-C3-001#cl-5.2 which mandates a minimum capacity of one kilowatt peak.
The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 mandates a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW.

The system capacity is 12.00 kWp, which is below the 20 kW threshold where check meters become mandatory. | The cited clause regarding meter accuracy classes does not support the rejection based on missing check meters.
The rule states check meters are mandatory only for systems > 20 kW, but this system is 12 kWp.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 Amendment (DL-C3-015) which allows two changes per financial year instead of one. | The application complies with the updated rule allowing two changes per year and provides three months' notice, exceeding the two-month requirement.
The rule limits changes to twice per financial year, and the application has already made two changes, meaning this third request is prohibited.

The generator cited an outdated 2019 clause instead of the 2024 amendment which limits capacity to 5 times the sanctioned load. | The 2024 amendment (DL-C3-009) governs capacity limits for GNM and should have been applied to verify the 90kWp proposal against the 120kW sanctioned load.
The waiver applies only to 11kV and below networks, but this project uses a 33 kV connection. | The cumulative capacity for BRPL is 50 MW, which is below the 75 MW threshold for the waiver.

The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-015, which updated the cumulative capacity thresholds for TPDDL. | The application date is 2026-04-28; under the updated DL-C3-015, the TPDDL threshold is 100 MW, and the current cumulative capacity is 105 MW, supporting rejection.

The 2015 regulations (UP-C3-001) are superseded by the 2019 regulations (UP-C3-002) which allow up to 75% transformer capacity. | Under the 2019 rule, 125kW/160kVA is 78.1%, exceeding the 75% limit, but the generator cited the wrong, outdated 15% rule.
The cited clause's capacity limits are superseded by the 2024 amendment (DL-C3-009#cl-3.8) which allows capacity up to 5 times the sanctioned load.

The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit (500 kW) specified in the applicable DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 guidelines. | The generator failed to consider the 2024 amendment limiting GNM capacity to 5 times the sanctioned load.
The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit of 500 kW (100 kW * 5) allowed under the cited clause.

The generator approved the application based on SDO verification, but the technical feasibility outcome is still 'Not communicated by the licensee'. | The rule stating installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a report should have been used to justify approval despite the pending status.

The clause was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2, which makes VNM applicable to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The proposed 150 kWp capacity is within the 5x sanctioned load limit (20 kW * 5 = 100 kW, but the rule allows up to 10 MW).
The cited clause expands VNM applicability to all consumers, which contradicts the generator's decision to reject the VNM request.

The cited clause states MSME capacity is irrespective of sanctioned load, contradicting the rejection based on a 50% limit. | This clause explicitly removes capacity restrictions for captive consumers, which supports the 80kW proposal for a 100kW load.
The generator approved the application based on a rule for systems >20kW, but the proposed capacity is 18.00 kWp, making check meters optional.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal stating 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided', which violates the requirement for systems >17.5 kW.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but the correct threshold for check meters in Karnataka per KA-C5-001#cl-15 is 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider KA-C5-001#cl-15, which mandates a check meter for this 30kWp system.

The cumulative capacity (85 kW) is within the transformer limit (100 kVA), but the generator failed to apply the 65% peak capacity limit from GJ-C3-001. | The 65% cumulative capacity limit rule was not considered, which would likely block the application as 85 kW exceeds 65% of 100 kVA.
The cumulative capacity (70 kW) exceeds the 65% threshold of the 100 kVA transformer (65 kW) specified in the primary regulation GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso.

The application is still in the 'Technical Feasibility' stage and the outcome is 'Not communicated', so it cannot be approved yet. | The 9kWp proposal is deemed feasible under Note ii, but the generator failed to consider this rule to justify the status.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal stating 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided', which violates the requirement for systems >17.5 kW.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider KA-C5-001#cl-15, which mandates a check meter for this 35kWp system.

The original 0.2s accuracy requirement in GJ-C3-001 was superseded by the 2020 amendment GJ-C3-003. | The amendment allows 1.0 accuracy for Solar Generation Meters, which matches the EPC proposal, making the rejection invalid.

The proposed meters (1.0 and 0.5S) meet the accuracy requirements specified in the cited clause. | The system capacity is 25 kWp, making a check meter mandatory, but the rejection reason focuses on accuracy rather than the missing check meter.
The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing up to 999 KW, yet the application is rejected despite being a domestic consumer with 8.0 kW sanctioned load.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability. | The generator used an outdated restrictive definition instead of the current broad applicability for all NCT Delhi consumers.
The proposed 120 kWp capacity significantly exceeds the consumer's sanctioned load of 30.0 kW, which may violate capacity-to-load ratios under VNM guidelines.
Cumulative solar capacity (55 kW) is 55% of transformer capacity (100 kVA), which is within the 65% limit, but the decision is approved despite the rule being a constraint.

The cumulative solar capacity (55.0 kW) is well within the transformer capacity (100 kVA), so the proviso does not mandate approval or rejection based on capacity limits. | The generator failed to consider the 65% peak capacity limit rule which is the actual governing threshold for transformer loading.
The cumulative capacity for BRPL is 95 MW, which exceeds the 75 MW limit specified in the cited clause for SLD waiver.
The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing up to 999 KW, yet the application is rejected despite being a domestic consumer with 4.0 kW load.

The transformer capacity limit is 15% (15 kVA), but current solar is 72 kVA (72%), which exceeds the limit, making the rejection correct but the cited rule is superseded by UP-C3-002. | The 2019 regulations (UP-C3-002) allow up to 75% capacity, and since current solar is 72%, the application should be accepted under the newer rule.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 Amendment (DL-C3-015) which allows two changes per year instead of one. | While the 2025 amendment allows two changes, the application only provided one month's notice instead of the required two months.
The cited clause states claims after October 2024 are not entertained, but the regulatory evidence clarifies all Phase II applications are admissible if claims are received by 31.12.2025.

The cumulative capacity for TPDDL under this rule is 50 MW, but the portal shows 120 MW, exceeding the waiver threshold. | The 2025 amendment is effective from 2026-01-20, but the application uses an outdated 2024 rule threshold.
The cumulative capacity for TPDDL is 120 MW, which exceeds the 100 MW waiver threshold specified in the cited clause.
The generator cites a 0.2s accuracy requirement, but the 2020 amendment (GJ-C3-003) updated the requirement to 0.5S or better, which the application meets.

The decision is premature because the technical feasibility outcome has not yet been communicated by the licensee as required by this clause. | The generator failed to consider that installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible, which would support an approval if the feasibility stage were complete.
The cited clause states claims after October 2024 are not entertained, but the clarifying note says all Phase II applications are admissible if claims are received by 31.12.2025.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The decision fails to account for the 5x sanctioned load limit (30kW * 5 = 150kW) which the 200kWp proposal exceeds.

The cited clause actually permits Virtual Net Metering for all consumers, which supports the user's request rather than justifying a rejection. | The clause allows ground-mounted capacity up to 5 times the sanctioned load, and 200kWp is within the 150kW limit (30kW * 5).
